clue.text: He settles punctuation first

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark
first is abbreviated 1ST, and the digit 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A man arranges his punctuation before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives 1ST, with the figure 1 standing in for the letter I, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist is a settler who makes a home in a new territory.

clue.text: Wheel on the furniture oil

explanation.surface: Lubricating the wheels of a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A caster is a small swivelling wheel on a chair leg; castor oil is a vegetable purgative oil.

clue.text: She washes the French strip

parts.note: la is a French word for the
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman taking her clothes off to bathe.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman who washes clothes for a living.

clue.text: Subject is a change into system of state control

parts.note: a national is a subject or citizen of a country
taken as written

indicators.note: change asks for the letters of the following word to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A topic gets transformed into government ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationalisation brings industries into public ownership under the government.

clue.text: Unaccompanied maiden available for ruler (very wise!) ()

parts.note: a solo is performed without accompaniment
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
on means available, as in on offer

explanation.surface: A single young woman is free for a sage king.
explanation.definitionFit: Solomon, the biblical king of Israel, is famed for his wisdom.

clue.text: Conditions made by sovereign territories

explanation.surface: Some terms are laid down by independent nations.
explanation.definitionFit: A state is a condition (a state of repair) and also a self-governing nation.

clue.text: People agree on technique for painting in an emotional manner

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after the following piece

parts.note: tempera is painting with pigment bound in egg
men means people
to tally is to agree, match up

explanation.surface: Artists see eye to eye about a painting method, but passionately.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperamentally means moodily, governed by changeable feelings.

clue.text: Keep wet or unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled means the preceding letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to stay damp or upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the main fortified building of a castle, often a great tower.

clue.text: Warder heard metallic sound: making minute investigation

indicators.note: heard says the warder word is spoken, keeping only its sound

parts.note: screw is prison slang for a warder

indicators.note: sound again asks for a word as spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: metallic, of a thin clanking quality, is tinny

explanation.surface: A prison guard hears clanking and starts a close inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' makes SCREW sound as SCRU, and 'sound' makes TINNY sound as TINY: said together they give SCRUTINY.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutiny is close, detailed examination.

clue.text: Double over for example: back pain

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: a twin is a double

indicators.note: back means the preceding abbreviation is reversed

explanation.surface: Bending over gives someone a sore back.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a sudden sharp pang.

clue.text: Prevent development of anything spectacular

explanation.surface: Someone holds back the growth of anything showy.
explanation.definitionFit: To stunt is to check growth; a stunt is also an attention-grabbing feat or display.

clue.text: Fabric requiring, it must be said, additional cutting machinery'

parts.note: lawn is a fine linen or cotton cloth

indicators.note: a phrase about speaking, so the next word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: additional means more

explanation.surface: A piece of cloth apparently needs further cutting equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent MORE and MOWER sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawnmower is a machine for cutting grass.

clue.text: Not even postman is casual worker

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
a post is a job, so a post-man becomes a job-man

explanation.surface: The postman, irregular in hours, is only employed occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'postman' is split: POST means a job, then MAN stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd-job man does miscellaneous small tasks on an occasional basis.

clue.text: Feel sorry about abandoning river bird

indicators.note: abandoning means the following piece is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: to feel sorry about something is to regret it

explanation.surface: Someone regrets walking away from a waterside bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are white herons that wade in marshes and shallows.

clue.text: Engineers mainstay

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers are the backbone of the operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs 'main stay' together as 'mainstay'; the wordplay needs MAIN and then the definition 'stay'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay somewhere is to be left there, not depart.

clue.text: Commotion about authorised version all goes back to prevarication

indicators.note: all of the assembled letters are then read backwards
about means the next piece is surrounded by the commotion word

parts.note: noise is a din or commotion
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A fuss over the King James Bible ends in everyone dodging the issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the container NOISAVE, and 'all goes back' reverses the whole of it, not just the last piece; the Authorised Version is the King James Bible of 1611.
explanation.definitionFit: Prevarication is speaking evasively to avoid the truth.

clue.text: Virus has lot of impact on South Africa's registration

indicators.note: a lot of the word, not all of it, drops its final letters

parts.note: influence means impact or effect
ZA is the international vehicle registration code for South Africa

explanation.surface: A virus much affects car registrations in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Influenza, flu, is a disease caused by a virus.

clue.text: Supporter has bad head gash

indicators.note: bad signals the following word's letters are mangled

parts.note: a rent is a tear or gash

explanation.surface: A fan has a nasty cut on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or backer of a cause.

clue.text: Do it slowly initially, to avoid fire

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the three preceding words

parts.note: to miss something is to avoid it

explanation.surface: Advice to go gently at first so as to escape being shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire an employee is to sack or discharge them.

clue.text: Archbishop is about to give an indication

indicators.note: about turns the preceding pieces around to read backwards

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury

explanation.surface: A senior cleric is about to make a gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it reverses LANGIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To signal is to make a sign or gesture conveying a message.

clue.text: Something unrepeatable about English cricket side

parts.note: on means about, concerning
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A remark on a team playing English cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the off side is the half of the field facing the batter's bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is a unique event that will not happen again.

clue.text: Several deliveries, every one of working gear

parts.note: an over in cricket is six balls bowled
every means all

explanation.surface: Many parcels arrive, each of them work clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: An overall is a protective garment worn for work.

clue.text: Vein runs through slice of meat

indicators.note: through means the first piece goes into the middle of the meat word

parts.note: a steak is a slice of meat
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A thread of fat goes through a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak is a line or seam of a different colour or material.

clue.text: Spherical container for plant

indicators.note: the word that follows holds the answer inside its letters

explanation.surface: A round pot for growing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the genus of heaths and heathers, low flowering shrubs.

clue.text: Force (Northern Ireland) rise to encounter

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the pieces read upwards

parts.note: the RUC, Royal Ulster Constabulary, was Northern Ireland's police force

explanation.surface: The Northern Irish police meet growing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost is to meet with or run into it.

clue.text: Elderly relative is fantastic, social worker stated

parts.note: fantastic means great

indicators.note: stated says the preceding word is spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect in a social colony

explanation.surface: An old relation is wonderful, according to a care worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' wants a welfare official; it is an ant, which in British speech can sound like AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-aunt is a parent's aunt, typically of an older generation.

clue.text: Arrange deal with China to produce food in Mexico

indicators.note: arrange tells you to put the letters of the following words into a new order

explanation.surface: Negotiating a trade agreement with Beijing to bring dishes to Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish of a filled, rolled tortilla in sauce.

clue.text: Spike without point used as weapon by cavalry

definitions.text: Spike without point used as weapon by cavalry

parts.words: Spike without point used as weapon by cavalry
parts.note: a long pointed shaft carried by mounted soldiers; 'without' read as 'on the outside', since its point sticks out ahead of the rider

explanation.surface: A blunt spike being wielded by horsemen.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by mounted soldiers.

clue.text: Press whip-round? Right!

indicators.note: round places the whip word around the next piece

parts.note: a thong is a leather whip lash

explanation.surface: A newspaper collection for a colleague gets approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip-round' looks like a collection of money, but 'round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A press of people is a dense crowd.

clue.text: Quietly relaxed to run through recording

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
lay back means reclined, relaxed

explanation.surface: A calm instruction to listen through a tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Playback is the replaying of recorded sound or video.
